newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela to hold talks on future IMF agreement.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to hold talks on future IMF agreement.

text.p: Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar will travel to Washington next week to hold talks with the IMF on a future program to follow its current standby agreement, Venezuelan ambassador Pedro Luis Echeverria said Thursday.
Echeverria told reporters that Matos would discuss with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus how to continue the one-year agreement signed in July.

Echeverria said Venezuela, which only drew down a $500 million tranche of the $1.4 billion standby agreement, does not need the IMF's money but rather its technical assistance and its overall blessing.
"We have several options to continue our program with the IMF," Echeverria said. "It could be an extended fund facility, or it could be a shadow program."
Venezuela would require the IMF's support to tap other loans from the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank for structural and social program reforms, Echeverria said.
Venezuela plans to overhaul its social security system and to slim down its bloated public sector under a second stage of reforms.

Long a holdout among Latin America's major economies, Venezuela adopted a tough fiscal adjustment program last year after failing to stabilize its economy through state price and interest rate controls.

Since it launched its "Agenda Venezuela" program, Venezuela's economy started to mend after years of recession. Echeverria said his government expected gross domestic product to grow by four percent in 1997, up from last year's slight contraction.

He said that inflation is forecast to drop to about 25 percent this year from about 100 percent in 1996. He added that Venezuela's foreign reserves are flush with cash, largely due to the increase in oil prices. Venezuela is a leading oil exporters.
